subtitle: How a Gond king sought the language of the gods

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of a forested hill-fort court
panels.action: Sangram Shah stands on a stone terrace of Garha-Katanga's fort, clad in royal attire, facing a dignified Brahmin poet Bhanudatta Misra who holds a palm-leaf manuscript, while beyond them rise dense forests and temple spires in hazy light.

dialogue.text: In the thick forests of Garha-Katanga, Gond king Sangram Shah and poet Bhanudatta Miśra forged a court where Sanskrit—the language of gods—became a weapon of power.

i18n.hi: गढ़-कटंगा के घने जंगलों में गोंड राजा संग्राम शाह और कवि भानुदत्त मिश्र ने ऐसा दरबार गढ़ा जहाँ देवभाषा संस्कृत ही ताकत का हथियार बनी।

panels.shot: epic bird’s-eye view over central Indian plateau
panels.action: A wide view of central India shows winding rivers, rugged hills, and the fortified city of Garha-Katanga emerging from forest, with a small Gond cavalry column riding along dusty paths below.

dialogue.text: Early sixteenth-century Central India was a patchwork of forts and forests, of Malwa sultans, Rajput chiefs, and Gond rulers like Sangram Shah in Garha-Katanga.

i18n.hi: सोलहवीं सदी की शुरुआत में मध्य भारत किलों और जंगलों का जाल था—मालवा के सुलतान, राजपूत सरदार, और गढ़-कटंगा में संग्राम शाह जैसे गोंड शासक।

panels.action: Inside a pillared audience hall with carved wooden beams and simple yet dignified decor, Sangram Shah sits on a low throne surrounded by Gond nobles, while a Brahmin priest recites from a palm-leaf manuscript near a lit brass lamp.

dialogue.text: Colonial writers later called such Gond kings mere forest chiefs, as if their courts knew no books, no ritual, no subtle speech. But inscriptions and texts whisper another story.

i18n.hi: अंग्रेज़ी राज के लेखकों ने गोंड राजाओं को बस जंगल के मुखिया कहा, मानो उनके दरबार में न किताबें हों, न अनुष्ठान, न महीन बोल। पर शिलालेख और ग्रंथ एक अलग कहानी फुसफुसाते हैं।

panels.shot: close-up on Sangram Shah’s thoughtful face
panels.action: Sangram Shah leans slightly forward on his throne, brow furrowed yet eyes bright, listening intently as a court scholar gestures toward a palm-leaf manuscript placed on a low stand.

dialogue.text: Sangram Shah ruled roughly from 1513 to 1543. Around him, a new game of prestige was unfolding—one played not only with spears and forts, but with verses and rituals.

i18n.hi: संग्राम शाह ने लगभग १५१३ से १५४३ तक राज किया। उनके आस-पास प्रतिष्ठा की नई बाज़ी चल रही थी—जो सिर्फ भालों और किलों से नहीं, श्लोकों और विधियों से भी खेली जाती थी।

panels.action: A split composition shows three courts: a Deccan sultan receiving scholars, a Rajput ruler listening to a Sanskrit recitation, and Sangram Shah in Garha-Katanga, all linked by faint, flowing script-like patterns in the air.

dialogue.text: Across the subcontinent, rulers embraced Sanskrit as a language of gods and kings. Supporting its poets could weave a Gond kingdom into these vast courtly networks.

i18n.hi: पूरा उपमहाद्वीप में शासक संस्कृत को देवों और राजाओं की भाषा मानकर अपनाते थे। उसके कवियों को सहारा देकर गोंड राज्य भी इन विशाल दरबारी जालों में जुड़ सकता था।

panels.shot: intimate interior, slow push-in on a manuscript chest
panels.action: In a quiet chamber lit by a single oil lamp, an attendant opens a wooden chest to reveal neatly stacked palm-leaf bundles, while Bhanudatta Misra, in simple scholar’s robes, carefully lifts one manuscript.

dialogue.text: Among the names linked to Sangram Shah’s court is Bhanudatta Miśra, a learned Brahmin whose Rasamañjarī would become a celebrated Sanskrit treatise on poetic taste and love.

i18n.hi: संग्राम शाह के दरबार से जुड़ा एक नाम है भानुदत्त मिश्र, विद्वान ब्राह्मण, जिसकी ‘रसमान्जरी’ काव्य-सु_vk और प्रेम पर प्रसिद्ध संस्कृत ग्रंथ बनी।

panels.shot: medium shot of their first meeting in court
panels.action: In the audience hall, Bhanudatta Misra stands with joined palms before Sangram Shah, who gestures for him to rise, while nearby courtiers watch with a mix of curiosity and respect.

dialogue.text: Later scholars connect Bhanudatta to Garha-Katanga, reading his verses as threads tying a Sanskrit poet’s journey to a Gond king’s ambitions.

i18n.hi: बाद के विद्वान भानुदत्त को गढ़-कटंगा से जोड़ते हैं, उसकी पंक्तियों में संस्कृत कवि की यात्रा को गोंड राजा की महत्वाकांक्षाओं से बंधती डोरियाँ पढ़ते हैं।

panels.action: Bhanudatta Misra stands poised, one hand slightly raised, reciting from a palm-leaf while Sangram Shah and his assembled nobles sit attentive; the hall’s air seems to vibrate with invisible syllables.

dialogue.text: In works like the Rasamañjarī, Bhanudatta refined rasas—flavours of emotion—that poets and patrons cherished. To host such a voice was to claim a place in that refined world.

i18n.hi: रसमान्जरी जैसे ग्रंथों में भानुदत्त ने रसों—भावों के स्वाद—को पैना किया, जिन्हें कवि और आश्रयदाता दोनों संभाल कर रखते थे। ऐसे स्वर को ठहराना उस सुसंस्कृत दुनिया में हिस्सा माँगना था।

panels.action: After court, Sangram Shah walks alongside Bhanudatta Misra in a palace courtyard, shaded by trees; the king gestures toward the horizon, while the poet listens, cradling his manuscript.

dialogue.speaker: Sangram Shah & Bhanudatta Miśra
dialogue.text: Let our forests also echo with the language of the gods.

i18n.hi: हमारे जंगल भी देवभाषा की गूँज से भरें।

panels.action: In a temple-like chamber, Brahmin ritual specialists perform a fire offering; Sangram Shah stands with folded hands, while Bhanudatta Misra watches, the scene framed by carved pillars and simple Vaishnava imagery.

dialogue.text: Ritual experts, often Vaiṣṇava, moved through such courts. Their rites, mantras, and praise verses could mark a Gond king as dharmic ruler, not only regional warlord.

i18n.hi: वैष्णव परंपरा के पंडित ऐसे दरबारों में घूमते थे। उनके अनुष्ठान, मंत्र और स्तुतियाँ गोंड राजा को सिर्फ सरहदी सरदार नहीं, धर्मशील राजधर्म पालन करने वाला दिखा सकते थे।

panels.shot: close-up on an inscription being carved
panels.action: A sculptor carefully chisels a Sanskrit inscription on stone, the emerging letters crisp and formal; behind him, a court official and Bhanudatta Misra supervise, while Sangram Shah watches from a short distance.

dialogue.text: Later Sanskrit inscriptions from the Gond realm show this world taking shape—names of gods and donors, kings and lineages, carved into stone by men of the forested plateau.

i18n.hi: गोंड भूभाग के बाद के संस्कृत शिलालेख दिखाते हैं कि यह संसार कैसे बन रहा था—देवताओं और दानदाताओं के नाम, राजा और वंश पत्थर पर खुदे, वन-पठार के लोगों के हाथों।

panels.action: Sangram Shah, unusually without full regalia, sits on a mat beside Bhanudatta Misra in a lamplit study, listening as the poet traces a verse on a palm leaf with a stylus.

dialogue.text: Some later reports even attribute a medical text, the Rasratnamālā, to Sangram Shah. Scholars treat this cautiously, as attribution rather than firm proof of his authorship.

i18n.hi: कुछ बाद की रिपोर्टें तो ‘रसरत्नमाला’ नाम की औषध-विद्या पर ग्रंथ का श्रेय भी संग्राम शाह को देती हैं। विद्वान इसे सतर्क नज़र से देखते हैं—श्रेय मानते हैं, पक्की रचना नहीं।

panels.shot: medium on Bhanudatta teaching younger scribes
panels.action: Bhanudatta Misra sits before a small group of young scribes, demonstrating how to hold the stylus and palm leaf, while an older Gond noble looks on, arms folded, quietly approving.

dialogue.text: What we can see clearly is aspiration: a Gond court drawing in Brahmin scholars, commissioning texts, and training scribes to handle the delicate palm leaves of Sanskrit learning.

i18n.hi: जो साफ दिखता है वह है आकांक्षा—एक गोंड दरबार जो ब्राह्मण विद्वानों को बुला रहा है, ग्रंथ लिखवा रहा है, और संस्कृत ज्ञान की नाज़ुक ताड़-पत्तियों को सँभालने के लिए लिपिकार तैयार कर रहा है।

panels.action: The panel is split vertically: on one side Sangram Shah oversees armed men and elephants near a fortress wall; on the other, he stands in a small library where Bhanudatta Misra arranges manuscripts on a shelf.

dialogue.text: Fortresses and campaigns gave Sangram Shah territory. But poets and priests gave him another kind of map—of prestige and memory that stretched beyond his forests.

i18n.hi: किले और मुहिमों ने संग्राम शाह को इलाक़ा दिया। पर कवि और पुजारी उसे एक और नक्शा दे गए—यश और स्मृति का, जो उसके जंगलों से बहुत दूर तक फैलता था।

panels.shot: wide shot of a visiting scholar’s departure
panels.action: At the city gate, Bhanudatta Misra prepares to depart in an ox-cart, manuscripts carefully packed, while Sangram Shah stands on the rampart above, raising a hand in farewell as the road winds into the distance.

dialogue.text: In time, poets and pundits moved on to other patrons. Yet their references, dedications, and stories left traces of Garha-Katanga in the larger Sanskrit ecumene.

i18n.hi: समय के साथ कवि और पंडित अगले आश्रयदाताओं की ओर बढ़ गए। पर उनकी संदर्भों, समर्पणों और कथाओं ने बड़ी संस्कृत दुनिया में गढ़-कटंगा की हल्की-सी रेखा छोड़ दी।

panels.shot: modern historian’s-eye bird’s-eye over ruins and forests
panels.action: From high above, the worn ruins of Garha-Katanga peek through today’s forests; superimposed subtly in the scene, Sangram Shah and Bhanudatta Misra appear like faint figures of memory walking along the old walls.

dialogue.text: Later historians like Sheldon Pollock place courts such as Sangram Shah’s within a broad pattern, where Sanskrit patronage itself became a political act of claiming kingly rank.

i18n.hi: शेल्डन पोलॉक जैसे इतिहासकार संग्राम शाह के दरबार को उस बड़े पैटर्न में रखते हैं, जहाँ संस्कृत का आश्रय देना ही राज-प्रतिष्ठा का दावा करने की राजनीतिक चाल बन गया।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a single palm-leaf manuscript resting on stone
panels.action: A single, weathered palm-leaf manuscript rests on a rough stone ledge overlooking a forested valley at dusk, as if left there long ago; faint silhouettes of Sangram Shah and Bhanudatta Misra stand in the distant haze.

dialogue.text: To read Sangram Shah’s court through Bhanudatta Miśra’s world is to redraw the map of prestige: a Gond king using learning, not just war, to write his name into the language of the gods.

i18n.hi: भानुदत्त मिश्र की दुनिया से संग्राम शाह के दरबार को पढ़ना यश का नक्शा फिर से खींचना है—एक गोंड राजा जो सिर्फ युद्ध नहीं, विद्या से भी अपना नाम देवभाषा में दर्ज करा रहा था।

subtitle_i18n.en: How a Gond king sought the language of the gods
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे एक गोंड राजा ने देवभाषा को अपनाया
